TABLE.NAME: block_nvq_matrix_grades
TABLE.COMMENT: Unit-level assessor grades for the NVQ Competence Matrix. Fully separate from Exabis Competence Grid tables so evidence-upload auto-seeding and exacomp's own grading can never collide with this data.

FIELD.NAME: studentid
FIELD.COMMENT: The student being graded.

FIELD.NAME: topicid
FIELD.COMMENT: The exacomp topic (unit) this grade applies to.

FIELD.NAME: courseid
FIELD.COMMENT: The specific course this unit belongs to, so a grade never leaks across courses.

FIELD.NAME: value
FIELD.COMMENT: 1 = Competent, 0 = Not Yet Competent, NULL = no verdict set (grade cleared). NULL is distinct from the row not existing at all: a row can exist purely to hold a comment with no verdict.

FIELD.NAME: comment
FIELD.COMMENT: Optional assessor comment, visible to the student. Independent of value - clearing the grade verdict does not clear this.

FIELD.NAME: gradedby
FIELD.COMMENT: The assessor who last set the verdict (value). NULL when value is NULL.

FIELD.NAME: timemodified
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp the verdict (value) was last set. NULL when value is NULL.

FIELD.NAME: commentedby
FIELD.COMMENT: The assessor who last saved the comment. Tracked separately from gradedby so clearing the verdict never affects comment attribution.

FIELD.NAME: commenttime
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp shown against the comment. Normally the save time, but can be manually backdated by the assessor (e.g. grading a portfolio that was actually completed earlier).

INDEX.NAME: studentid-topicid-courseid
INDEX.COMMENT: One grade per student per unit per course — prevents duplicate rows entirely.

TABLE.NAME: block_nvq_matrix_sampling
TABLE.COMMENT: Per-unit IQA/EQA sampling status for the NVQ Competence Matrix. Editable only by editingteacher/manager; non-editing teacher (EQA role) is view-only.

FIELD.NAME: studentid
FIELD.COMMENT: The student whose unit is being sampled.

FIELD.NAME: topicid
FIELD.COMMENT: The exacomp topic (unit) this sampling status applies to.

FIELD.NAME: courseid
FIELD.COMMENT: The specific course this unit belongs to.

FIELD.NAME: status
FIELD.COMMENT: 0 = blank/not set, 1 = Sampled, 2 = Not Yet Sampled.

FIELD.NAME: sampledby
FIELD.COMMENT: The user who last set this status.

INDEX.NAME: studentid-topicid-courseid
INDEX.COMMENT: One sampling status per student per unit per course.

TABLE.NAME: block_nvq_matrix_evidence_comments
TABLE.COMMENT: Optional assessor comment attached to a single evidence item occurrence (one specific item-to-criterion link) in the NVQ Competence Matrix.

FIELD.NAME: studentid
FIELD.COMMENT: Owner of the evidence item.

FIELD.NAME: mmid
FIELD.COMMENT: block_exacompcompuser_mm row id - the specific item-to-criterion link this comment belongs to. The same evidence item can be linked to more than one criterion, each with its own mm row and therefore its own comment.

FIELD.NAME: itemid
FIELD.COMMENT: The exaport item ID this comment is attached to (stored for reference/lookup convenience only - mmid is the real key).

FIELD.NAME: evidencetype
FIELD.COMMENT: Short code for the evidence type: APL, EoE, NA, O, P, PD, Q, RA, S, WT. NULL = not set. Independent of the comment - editable by assessors and IQA, not just whoever wrote the comment.

INDEX.NAME: studentid-mmid
INDEX.COMMENT: One comment (and one evidence type) per item-to-criterion link per student.

TABLE.NAME: block_nvq_matrix_unit_comments
TABLE.COMMENT: Optional unit-level assessor comment and IQA comment for the NVQ Competence Matrix, each independent of grading/sampling and each recording who wrote it.

FIELD.NAME: studentid
FIELD.COMMENT: The student this unit's comments apply to.

FIELD.NAME: topicid
FIELD.COMMENT: The exacomp topic (unit) these comments apply to.

FIELD.NAME: courseid
FIELD.COMMENT: The specific course this unit belongs to, so a comment never leaks across courses.

FIELD.NAME: assessorcomment
FIELD.COMMENT: Optional assessor comment, independent of the grade verdict.

FIELD.NAME: assessorcommentby
FIELD.COMMENT: The user who last saved the assessor comment.

FIELD.NAME: assessorcommenttime
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp of the last assessor comment save.

FIELD.NAME: iqacomment
FIELD.COMMENT: Optional IQA comment, independent of the sampling status.

FIELD.NAME: iqacommentby
FIELD.COMMENT: The user who last saved the IQA comment.

FIELD.NAME: iqacommenttime
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp of the last IQA comment save.

INDEX.NAME: studentid-topicid-courseid
INDEX.COMMENT: One comment row (holding both the assessor comment and the IQA comment) per student per unit per course.

TABLE.NAME: block_nvq_matrix_status
TABLE.COMMENT: Final Pass/Fail status per student per course, set by the assessor once grading/IQA is complete, plus a record of when/if a completion notification was sent to the student. Deliberately separate from block_nvq_matrix_grades (unit-level) - this is the qualification-level outcome.

FIELD.NAME: studentid
FIELD.COMMENT: The student this final status applies to.

FIELD.NAME: courseid
FIELD.COMMENT: The specific course/qualification this final status applies to.

FIELD.NAME: status
FIELD.COMMENT: 1 = Pass, 0 = Fail, NULL = not yet set.

FIELD.NAME: setby
FIELD.COMMENT: The assessor who last set the status. NULL when status is NULL.

FIELD.NAME: timemodified
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp the status was last set. NULL when status is NULL.

FIELD.NAME: notifiedtime
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp the completion notification was last sent to the student. NULL if never sent. Sending is a deliberately unconstrained, repeatable action - not gated on any workflow state - so this is purely a record of the most recent send, not a one-shot flag.

FIELD.NAME: notifiedby
FIELD.COMMENT: The assessor who last triggered the notification.

INDEX.NAME: studentid-courseid
INDEX.COMMENT: One final status per student per course.

TABLE.NAME: block_nvq_matrix_evidence_types
TABLE.COMMENT: Evidence type classification(s) for a single evidence item occurrence (one row per selected type). One evidence item can genuinely fit more than one type (e.g. both Observation and Professional Discussion), so this is a proper one-to-many child table of block_nvq_matrix_evidence_comments rather than a single column - deliberately NOT joined directly against the main evidence query when building the matrix (that would multiply/misalign the parent evidence row once per matching type row); always fetched as a separate keyed lookup and merged in PHP, same pattern already used for block_nvq_matrix_sampling.

FIELD.NAME: evidencecommentid
FIELD.COMMENT: block_nvq_matrix_evidence_comments row id this type applies to.

FIELD.NAME: code
FIELD.COMMENT: One of: APL, EoE, NA, O, P, PD, Q, RA, S, WT.

INDEX.NAME: evidencecommentid-code
INDEX.COMMENT: Each type can only be selected once per evidence item - prevents duplicate rows.

TABLE.NAME: block_nvq_matrix_assessor
TABLE.COMMENT: The single designated Assessor for a course, chosen from that course's editing teachers. IQA and Assessor both map to the same underlying teacher/editingteacher role on this site, so this table is what actually distinguishes 'the assessor' for notification purposes - e.g. who gets notified when a student submits evidence. One row per course; set via the dropdown at the top of the matrix by anyone holding block/nvq_matrix:manageassessor (editingteacher, manager).

FIELD.NAME: courseid
FIELD.COMMENT: The course this assessor designation applies to. One assessor per course.

FIELD.NAME: userid
FIELD.COMMENT: The designated assessor. Must be a user holding block/nvq_matrix:grade in this course at the time they're set - enforced by matrix_data::save_assessor(), not by a DB constraint.

FIELD.NAME: setby
FIELD.COMMENT: The editingteacher/manager who made this designation.

FIELD.NAME: timemodified
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp this designation was last set/changed.

INDEX.NAME: courseid
INDEX.COMMENT: One designated assessor per course - saving again for the same course updates the existing row rather than inserting a second one. Deliberately no separate courseid foreign key in KEYS above - a real live upgrade attempt confirmed Moodle's xmldb_table rejects a KEY and an INDEX on the identical field set as a collision regardless of what either is named (renaming the index to 'courseid-unique' alone did NOT fix it - the second attempt hit the same rejection, just naming the index instead of the key in the error). Every other unique index in this file (e.g. evidencecommentid-code on block_nvq_matrix_evidence_types) pairs a foreign key with a unique index on a DIFFERENT, wider field combination - there's no working precedent anywhere in this plugin for a foreign key and a unique index on the exact same single field together. Moodle doesn't enforce FK referential integrity at the DB engine level regardless (it's advisory metadata only), so dropping the declared foreign key here costs nothing functionally - courseid validity is already guaranteed by context_course::instance($courseid) being called before any write in matrix_data::save_assessor().

TABLE.NAME: block_nvq_matrix_notified_items
TABLE.COMMENT: Tracks which eportfolio items (block_exaportitem.id) have already triggered an assessor-submission notification. Only ever consulted when the block_nvq_matrix/renotifyonedit admin setting is OFF ('once per item') - when it's ON (the default, matching the original behaviour), classes/task/notify_assessors_task.php never reads or writes this table at all, so leaving the setting on the default costs nothing extra.

FIELD.NAME: itemid
FIELD.COMMENT: block_exaportitem.id that has already been notified about at least once.

FIELD.NAME: timenotified
FIELD.COMMENT: Unix timestamp of the first (and, under 'once per item' mode, only) notification for this item.

INDEX.NAME: itemid
INDEX.COMMENT: One 'already notified' record per item. Deliberately no separate itemid foreign key - same reasoning as block_nvq_matrix_assessor's courseid index: a KEY and an INDEX on the identical single field collide in Moodle's xmldb_table regardless of naming, confirmed the hard way on that table already. No REFTABLE relationship declared for the same reason - block_exaportitem lives in a different plugin (block_exaport) entirely, so a formal foreign key across plugin boundaries isn't meaningful here regardless.
